input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: § 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day on Customer for any delay in providing a dependency — a Customer-payable liquidated amount triggered by even a minor or trivial delay, with no cap. That fails the fallback (which permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) and sits in walk-away territory because the per-day accrual is unbounded and can exceed remaining contract value. No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum-fee-on-termination provision appears in the document, and there are no offsetting service credits. We therefore take the preferred position and replace the charge in § 7.6 with a statement that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties; the edit is surgical and no other clause cross-references § 7.6, so no retained machinery contemplates such a payment.

ops.oldText: pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency
ops.newText: pay no liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we pay no liquidated damages or penalties, so we have replaced the USD 25,000 per day charge in § 7.6 with that statement; Vendor keeps its ordinary remedies for any genuine delay on our side. If a liquidated amount is unavoidable, we could consider only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable per-day liquidated damages in § 7.6 and confirm no LDs or penalties are payable by Customer.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
